title: Pear and almond cake
subtitle: French-style frangipane cake with ripe pears
excerpt: Pear and almond cake sets ripe pear halves into a light frangipane batter for a French-style dessert cake with a moist, almond-rich crumb. The pears soften into the batter as it bakes, releasing juice that keeps the crumb tender. Use pears that are ripe but still firm, or they will sink and release too much liquid.
sourceNotes: French tarte bourdaloue tradition documented in classic French patisserie manuals (public domain). Escoffier, Auguste (Le Guide Culinaire, 1903, public domain). Various British adaptations of frangipane cakes (public domain, 20th century).

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake up to 1 day ahead. Store loosely covered at room temperature.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Conventional oven, 170 degrees Celsius. Fan oven: 155 degrees Celsius. Bake on the middle shelf.
baking.decoratingTechnique: Fan-sliced pears arranged on top, apricot glaze finish

glossaryTerms.definition: A baked almond cream made from butter, sugar, eggs, and ground almonds in roughly equal proportions. It puffs up around fruit during baking and sets to a moist, tender crumb with a strong almond flavour. It is the filling in a Bakewell tart and the base of tarte bourdaloue. Frangipane is different from marzipan, which is uncooked and denser.

Beating softened butter and sugar together until the mixture is pale, light, and fluffy before adding eggs and flour. The process incorporates air into the fat, which helps the cake rise. The butter must be genuinely soft, not melted, for the method to work.

items.prepNote: ripe but firm; peeled, halved, and cored

content.text: Heat the oven to 170 degrees Celsius (conventional) or 155 degrees Celsius (fan). Grease a 23 cm round cake tin and line the base with baking paper.

Peel the pears, halve them from stem to base, and scoop out the core with a teaspoon. Place cut-side down on a board. Using a sharp knife, cut across each half in thin slices without cutting all the way through, leaving about 1 cm at the stem end intact, so the pear stays in one piece but fans when pressed.
Beat the butter and sugar together until pale and fluffy, about 3 to 4 minutes with a hand mixer. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well between additions. Beat in the vanilla extract.
Fold in the plain flour, ground almonds, and baking powder with a large silicone spatula until smooth. The batter will be thick. Spread it evenly into the prepared tin.

Arrange the pear halves on top of the batter, pressing each one in gently and fanning the slices as you go. Pack them closely; they will not all lie flat but will settle during baking. Scatter over the flaked almonds if using.

Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the batter is set and deep golden brown around the edges, and a skewer inserted into the almond sponge between the pears comes out clean. The centre may still feel slightly soft directly under a pear; that is the pear, not uncooked batter.

While the cake cools in the tin for 10 minutes, warm the apricot jam and water together in a small saucepan until loose. Push through a sieve if the jam has large pieces of fruit. Brush the glaze over the surface of the warm cake to give a sheen. Turn out onto a cooling rack. Serve at room temperature.

attrs.avoid: Avoid using pears that are overripe or very large.
attrs.fix: Very ripe pears are too soft and too heavy to stay on top of the batter. Use Conference or Bosc pears that give when pressed very lightly but still have some resistance. Cut them thinner if they are large varieties.

attrs.problem: Cake is wet in the centre after the suggested bake time
attrs.avoid: Avoid testing the cake directly under a pear half.
attrs.fix: Insert the skewer into the almond sponge between two pear halves. The pears release juice during baking, which can make the surrounding sponge take longer to set. Return to the oven in 5-minute increments until the skewer comes out clean.

attrs.problem: Flaked almonds burn before the cake is done
attrs.avoid: Avoid scattering flaked almonds over areas of exposed batter near the edge.
attrs.fix: Lay a sheet of baking paper loosely over the top of the tin after 25 minutes if the almonds are browning fast. Remove the paper for the final 5 minutes to crisp them slightly.
